Onpattro is the anchor because it matches on class and care setting: an siRNA, as del-brax's payload is, given by intravenous infusion on a fixed interval in the clinic under Part B, for a rare hereditary neuromuscular disease of adults that ends in lost mobility. Its 2022 figure, from 338 beneficiaries, was $290,245 (drug_demand), so the thin 2025 count does not move it far. Alternatives from the same file: Amvuttra $269,961.98 (2,861, diluted by its 2025 cardiomyopathy launch), Vyvgart IV $251,442.79 and Vyvgart Hytrulo $289,747.86 (1,798 and 1,789, generalised myasthenia and CIDP). The case for lower: FSHD's pool is several times DMD44's, which argues against an ultra-rare price. Novartis has disclosed no price

column11: Grabich et al., J Comp Eff Res 2025, doi:10.57264/cer-2025-0037 (Inovalon claims 2016 to 2024, 397 patients on the weekly intravenous oligonucleotides for Duchenne muscular dystrophy): median time to a first gap of 60 days or more was 25.5 months, and 110 of the 190 who had such a gap (57.9%) restarted. At a constant hazard 1 - 0.5^(12/25.5) = 27.83% open a gap each year, and 42.1% of those do not come back: 0.2783 x 0.421 = 11.72% stop a year. The nearest measured analogue: a chronic intravenous oligonucleotide in a muscular dystrophy, bought in the US
column12: Judgement on the analogue. The case for more stopping: Hong et al. (JAMA Netw Open 2024) found about a third of routine-care patients stopped the same drugs within a year, and adults on nusinersen in Valencia stopped at 75% over a median 4.6 years (J Neurol 2026, PMC13315468), mostly for treatment burden. The case for less: FORTITUDE had no discontinuations at 12 months (Novartis Avidity deck, 2025-10-27, p17), del-brax is dosed every six weeks rather than weekly, and adults on nusinersen before any alternative existed stopped at 5.5% a year (Elman et al., J Neuromuscul Dis 2022, 7 of 86 over a median 1.5 years)
